explanations: withTimeout() only aborts the AbortSignal when time is up, then keeps awaiting the work. That works for the HTTP carriers, whose transport rejects when the signal fires. Midwest Freight's callback-based SDK ignores the signal, so its promise never settles and withTimeout never returns, which stalls Promise.allSettled and the whole checkout. A timeout must stop waiting on its own and can't rely on the callee cooperating. The fix rejects with TimeoutError when the timer fires and still aborts the signal so cancellable work can clean up. It clears the timer when the work settles first.
